recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Do not add xhtml to the core Extension.value[x] choices for FHIR-8049. If broader XHTML-bearing extension values are desired, raise a new current-scope issue, likely involving the Extension Pack rendering extensions.
issue_request: FHIR-8049 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core request from the DSTU1 era to support rich XHTML-like narrative content in extensions. The Jira record includes a reopened resolution to create a markdown datatype, document graceful fallback, use it for extensions and ElementDefinition, and residual wording about exposing xhtml for Extension.
initial_application: The exact Jira-tagged implementation is git commit 05495454879b7561aecb912e59d065b6354b4681, which added markdown datatype documentation and markdown to the extension type list, plus companion commit a3551b9aeacb5ad61ce1d34b06ab7a62fa493d5c adding Java MarkdownType. No FHIR-8049-tagged commit added xhtml as a normal Extension.value[x] type.
additional_context: The current build-scope Extension source is active through source/fhir.ini and source/datatypes/extension.xml. Current generated CI output expands Extension.value[x] to include markdown and exclude xhtml. Later decisions FHIR-34314, FHIR-9693, FHIR-38714, and FHIR-20853 clarify that xhtml is special narrative/rendering content, markdown is the safe rich-text datatype, and datatype subtypes are not implicitly substitutable.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding valueXhtml to Extension.value[x] for this historical issue would contradict the original applied commit and later datatype/rendering-extension decisions.

related_jiras.note: Created rendering-xhtml and rendering-markdown extensions for string display markup, showing that XHTML extension content is handled by a specific rendering extension mechanism.
Clarified xhtml as special narrative content with narrative-page documentation rather than an ordinary datatype to add to Extension.value[x].
Tightened markdown to prohibit inline/raw HTML, supporting the safe rich-text interpretation of FHIR-8049.
Clarified that datatype subtypes are not substitutable unless explicitly listed, so markdown's inclusion and xhtml's exclusion are meaningful.
